blocks.text: Matt Dee, the former Bondi Rescue lifeguard who appeared on the show from 2008 to 2017, has died. His death was announced on the morning of Wednesday 2 September 2026 on the Instagram page of FTW Revolution, the suicide-prevention clothing label he co-founded and ran. His cause of death has not been made public.

A public celebration of his life is being held at Bronte Beach on Saturday 12 September 2026 from midday, with a paddle-out, and anyone who wants to come has been told they are welcome. Details are below.

items.label: Public memorial
items.value: Bronte Beach, Saturday 12 September 2026, from midday

blocks.text: Matt Dee's memorial at Bronte Beach: what we know

The send-off is a public one. It is being held at Bronte Beach on Saturday 12 September 2026, starting at midday, and it was announced by the North Maroubra Surf Riders rather than by his family - which tells you something about the crowd he belonged to. There is a paddle-out, his ashes are being spread in the water, and afterwards there is food, drink, music and the part everyone actually comes for, which is standing around telling stories about him.

Next Saturday, we send off a true legend. A man that had time for everyone, a larrikin, a brother to all and a leader of men. His time with us has come to an end, but we owe it to him to send him off in style.

One practical thing, because people will get this wrong: the memorial is at Bronte Beach, not Bondi Beach. Bronte is the next-but-one beach south, about 2 km down the coast, and the walk from Bondi along the clifftop path takes 25-30 minutes at an easy pace. There is very little parking at Bronte at the best of times and none worth hunting for on a Saturday with a crowd coming, so walk it from Bondi or take the 379 bus. If you are paddling out, you need your own board.

A paddle-out, if you have not seen one, is the surfing world's funeral rite: everyone paddles out past the break, forms a circle sitting on their boards, and there is usually a moment of quiet, some splashing of water and a lot of hollering. It is not solemn in the church sense. It is loud, and it is meant to be.

A fundraiser was also set up to cover the funeral and farewell costs, which had passed $12,500 of an $18,000 goal when Yahoo Lifestyle reported on it on 7 September. Donations had been made in the names of the Bondi Rescue lifeguard Harrison Reid and the boxer Harry Garside, among hundreds of others.
What happened to Matt Dee

The announcement came from FTW Revolution, the clothing and events brand he co-founded as a suicide-prevention resource aimed at young Australians. It was posted on the Wednesday morning alongside a photograph of him laughing, head thrown back, holding a beer - which is, by every account posted since, exactly how the people who knew him want him remembered.

It is with the heaviest of hearts that we share the heartbreaking news of the passing of our Matt Dee. Matt touched the lives of many, he also did amazing work and he will be deeply missed and forever remembered by those who knew and loved him.

The same statement asked for patience with messages and pointed anyone struggling with the news toward support. No cause of death has been confirmed in the nine days since, and until his family chooses to say more there is nothing further to report on that - so this page will not speculate.
Who Matt Dee was

Dee was on Bondi Rescue for nine seasons, from 2008 to 2017 - long enough that if you watched the show through its most-watched years, you knew his face. The lifeguards on that show are not actors: they are the professional beach lifeguards who work this stretch of sand every day, and Dee was one of them through a period when the show turned an ordinary Australian workplace into something people watched in more than a hundred countries.

He grew up in Melbourne, raised with his brother and sister by their single mother, and the family holidayed at Torquay - which is where he learned to surf, and how a Victorian kid ends up working the busiest beach in New South Wales.
The work he did off the beach

What Dee became known for after the show is harder to watch than any rescue on it. He lost both of his siblings within about a year of each other. His older brother Jonathan, who lived with bipolar disorder, died at 34. His younger sister Rachel Bridger Dee, who had lived with schizophrenia for around a decade, died in December 2009 at 30.
He spoke about them publicly rather than privately, which is a choice, and not an easy one. In a 2011 interview with The Sun-Herald he was blunt about how he wanted his brother and sister understood:

What happened was not their fault. They did their best to manage their illnesses. It wasn't their fault. They had a problem inside their heads. It's something we don't understand. How would we know what it's like?

He became an ambassador for Suicide Prevention Australia and for the Schizophrenia Research Institute, and FTW Revolution - the label he co-founded around that advocacy - has raised at least $500,000 for Suicide Prevention Australia, according to the ABC. He described who it was built for in his own words: 'the underdogs in the trenches, the battlers in the dark places'.

He also spoke about carrying guilt over his siblings' deaths, and the feeling that he might have done more - which is worth recording, because it is the thing so many people left behind carry silently, and he said it out loud.
Tributes from the Bondi lifeguards

Tributes filled the announcement post within hours, including from the lifeguards he worked alongside and from the official Bondi Lifeguards account. Trent 'Maxi' Maxwell wrote 'Rest easy brother'. Ryan 'Whippet' Clark posted: 'Big love Matty Dee. You had a wild wide and you will be missed by many.' The NRL player Josh Dugan was among those paying tribute too. Among the hundreds of messages from people who only ever knew him through a television screen, the word that keeps coming back is that he was one of a kind.

blocks.title: If this is difficult to read
blocks.text: Matt Dee spent much of his life telling people that they did not have to sit with this on their own, so it would be wrong to write about him without saying the same thing. Lifeline Australia is available 24 hours a day on 13 11 14, or by text on 0477 13 11 14. Beyond Blue is on 1300 22 4636.

items.a: A public celebration of his life is being held on Saturday 12 September 2026 from midday at Bronte Beach in Sydney's eastern suburbs. It was announced by the North Maroubra Surf Riders and includes a paddle-out, with his ashes spread in the water, followed by food, drinks and music on the beach.

items.q: Is Matt Dee's memorial open to the public?
items.a: Yes. It was announced publicly with an open invitation - 'we are calling on everyone to get down to Bronte' - so anyone who wants to pay their respects is welcome. If you intend to join the paddle-out you will need to bring your own board.

items.q: Where is Bronte Beach, and how do I get there from Bondi?
items.a: Bronte is about 2 km south of Bondi Beach, two beaches down the coast, and it is a different suburb with a different postcode. The nicest way there is on foot along the Bondi to Bronte clifftop path, which takes 25-30 minutes. Parking at Bronte is limited on any weekend and will be far worse with a crowd, so walking or the bus is the better plan.

items.q: What happened to Matt Dee from Bondi Rescue?
items.a: Matt Dee died, with his death announced on the morning of 2 September 2026 on the Instagram page of FTW Revolution, the suicide-prevention label he co-founded. The announcement described him as someone who 'touched the lives of many'. A public celebration of his life follows at Bronte Beach on 12 September 2026.

items.q: What was Matt Dee's cause of death?
items.a: It has not been made public. No cause of death has been confirmed by his family or in any published report in the time since his death, and anything circulating beyond that is speculation.

His age has not been confirmed in Australian reporting of his death. One overseas entertainment site has published an age, but it is not corroborated by the ABC or any other outlet we would rely on, so we are not repeating it. His brother Jonathan died at 34 and his sister Rachel at 30.

items.q: When was Matt Dee on Bondi Rescue?
items.a: He appeared on Bondi Rescue from 2008 to 2017, nine seasons of the show.

It is a clothing and events brand that Matt Dee co-founded and ran as a suicide-prevention resource for young Australians, and which the ABC reports has raised at least $500,000 for Suicide Prevention Australia. He was an ambassador for Suicide Prevention Australia and for the Schizophrenia Research Institute, advocacy he took up after losing his brother and sister within about a year of each other.

items.q: Was Matt Dee still a Bondi lifeguard?
items.a: No - he is described in reports of his death as a former Bondi Rescue lifeguard, and his time on the show ran from 2008 to 2017. The lifeguards currently patrolling Bondi are employed year-round by Waverley Council.

blocks.text: The lifeguards on this beach do a job most people only see the dramatic end of. If you want to know who is out there now, and what the service actually does across a season, our guide to the Bondi Rescue lifeguards is the place to start - and the coastal walk that gets you from Bondi down to Bronte is here.
